name: packed-earth yard ground autotile: tamped reddish-brown earth with faint wheel rut, footprints, pebbles and straw, a slight earth bank shadow on the south edge and grass tufts creeping over the rim, lying flat on grass (top-down 3/4 RPG ground)
label: beodeul_yard/dirt

surfaces.part: grass tufts and rim over the edge
grass hole in the middle of the earth patch

answer.evidence: This is a flat, top-down ground autotile. The reddish-brown earth fills a large irregular region about 120 rows tall (rows 3-122) with ruts, footprints, pebbles and straw. The only south-facing element is a thin bank edge: a light edge row at about row 123 (x=131) or 122-123 (x=88), then dark shadow rows 124-125 and a dark green row 126. That is a 2-3 row lip or shadow strip, not a vertical face of 3 or more rows. Nothing stands up as an object, so the tile reads as a flat slab with a slight edge shadow.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a packed-earth autotile on grass. The earth ramp shows about 5 steps: a light rim highlight, a mid brown body, darker grain and speckle, a darker south-bank shadow, and a dark brown edge. The edge is a tinted dark brown beside the earth, with a dark green lean beside the grass tufts. This matches the measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so it is not a black sticker line. Measured density is 9 visible tones per tile against 3 for the reference grass and 7 for the paving, and near-flat coverage is only 3%. Pebbles, straw flecks, footprints and rim tufts break up the surface. The interior earth is fairly sparse and the grass around it is lightly textured, so texture reads as 'some' rather than fully rich. A careful artist would still accept it beside the references without it looking thinner or flatter.
